extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients and institutional administrators (PD/PIs, Signing Officials, Authorized Organization Representatives, grants management staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural requirements for administering NIH grants, including progress and financial reporting, recordkeeping, audits, invention and disclosure reporting, and research security requirements for senior/key personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR requirement when award not continued
rubrics_metrics.description: If an award is not made or the recipient does not submit an application for continued support, a final RPPR is required (see Final Research Performance Progress Report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final RPPR replaces the previous Final Progress Report for closeout; recipients must submit the F-RPPR to report Project Outcomes, which will be made publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding IC specifies progress reporting for construction grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH awarding IC will specify the requirements for progress reporting under construction grants or grants supporting both construction activities and non-construction activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must follow IC-specific instructions for reporting progress on construction, acquisition/modernization, major alteration/renovation, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commons ID requirement for progress reports
rubrics_metrics.description: For progress reports using the RPPR, the Commons ID requirement is part of the Participants Section and is required for the PD/PI(s) and those who worked on the project in a postdoctoral role. For undergraduate and graduate students supported on a particular research grant, a Commons ID is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undergraduate/Graduate/Postdoctoral roles have been added in eRA Commons; Graduate Student and Postdoctoral eRA Commons Roles should NOT be used for individuals submitting Individual Fellowships (use PD/PI) nor for those on institutional training grants reported via xTrain (use Trainee Role). A Commons ID is strongly encouraged but optional for other project personnel; a general Project Personnel role exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to implement Individual Development Plans (IDPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH encourages recipients to develop an institutional policy requiring that an Individual Development Plan (IDP) be implemented for every graduate student and postdoctoral researcher supported by any NIH grant and reportable on the progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting of IDP implementation is in RPPR Section B. Accomplishments, Question B.4 and in RPPR Section D. Participants or on PHS 2271. Do not include the actual IDP document; describe how IDPs are used to manage training.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP designation on Notices of Award
rubrics_metrics.description: The NoA will specify whether an award is subject to the Streamlined Non-Competing Award Process (SNAP). Awards routinely included are 'K' and 'R' awards (except R35); excluded commonly are centers, cooperative agreements, institutional training grants, non-Fast Track Phase I SBIR/STTR awards, clinical trials, P01, R35, and awards to individuals, though inclusion/exclusion can be grant-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards may be excluded from SNAP if they require close monitoring or the recipient has a pattern of failure to adhere to reporting/notification deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified annual progress reports under SNAP
rubrics_metrics.description: For SNAP awards, a streamlined version of the RPPR (replacing eSNAP) is used and does not include detailed budget information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress reports for SNAP awards are submitted using the streamlined RPPR module in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified Notice of Award (NoA) under SNAP
rubrics_metrics.description: Under SNAP, the GMO negotiates the direct costs for the entire competitive segment (or determines modules for modular awards) so annual budget submissions/negotiations are eliminated. SNAP NoAs are issued with only total direct and indirect costs awarded for the budget period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although categorical direct cost breakdowns are not awarded, recipients must allocate and account for costs by category according to applicable cost principles. Future year commitments reflect total cost commitments (direct plus indirect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified financial reporting for SNAP awards
rubrics_metrics.description: For awards under SNAP, an FFR is required only at the end of a competitive segment rather than annually. The FFR must be submitted within 120 days after the end of the competitive segment and must report cumulative support for the entire segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An FFR must be submitted whether or not a competing continuation award is made; if no further award is made this serves as the final FFR (see Closeout).

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP progress report submission deadlines and format
rubrics_metrics.description: All SNAP progress reports are due the 15th of the month preceding the month in which the budget period ends (extended to next business day if 15th is weekend/holiday). Paper submissions are not acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper SNAP reports will not be considered and recipients will be required to resubmit electronically. RPPR in eRA Commons provides screens and uploads; recipients may delegate authority to PD/PI to submit for SNAP awards (managed per PD/PI in eRA Commons and revocable). See the RPPR Instruction Guide for submission guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reports for multi-year funded (MYF) awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports for MYF awards are due annually on or before the anniversary of the budget/project period start date; the reporting period is the calendar year preceding the anniversary date. A progress report is not required during a no-cost extension unless required by the IC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MYRPPR link to upload becomes available two months before the anniversary date in eRA Commons. Progress reports must be completed by the PD/PI and submitted by a Signing Official (SO) or PD/PI with delegated authority. See eRA Commons User Guide Section 10.2 on delegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Research Performance Progress Report (F-RPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The F-RPPR has replaced the Final Progress Report for closeout; generally same format as annual RPPR and requires reporting on Project Outcomes, which will be publicly available (analogous to Project Summary/Abstract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type 2 applications under consideration require an Interim-RPPR; if Type 2 is funded NIH treats Interim-RPPR as the annual performance report for final year of previous competitive segment; if not funded, Interim-RPPR will be treated as the F-RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: PMS pre-population and certification for financial drawdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: PMS will pre-populate the cash transaction section of the FFR using recipient real-time cash advance information and adjust recipient-reported disbursements to equal cash advance drawdowns on non-closed sub-accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must certify at each drawdown whether the request is for reimbursement of actual expenditures or an advance for immediate disbursement and must assert award funds are used in compliance with award conditions and federal statutory requirements; filing a false claim may result in civil or criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial expenditure reports must be submitted via PMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of expenditures are required as documentation of financial status and NIH requires all financial expenditure reports to be submitted using the Payment Management System (PMS). Paper expenditure reports are not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eRA Commons and PMS allow viewing and electronic submission; expenditure data initially reviewed and accepted by FFR Reconciliation and Financial Closeout Support Center (FFR-C) and also reviewed by NIH IC grants management staff. Except for SNAP and awards requiring more frequent reporting, FFR is required annually and must be submitted no later than 90 days after the end of the calendar quarter in which the budget period ended. Failure to submit timely reports may affect future funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and certification of FFRs before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting FFRs, recipients must ensure information is accurate, complete, and consistent with the recipient’s accounting system. The AOR or designated submitter certifies the FFR is correct and complete and represents a claim to the Federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a false claim may result in civil or criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions for indirect cost changes and revised expenditure reports
rubrics_metrics.description: FFRs must reflect the proper amount of indirect costs applicable to the grant period. If provisional or earlier permanent rates are used and a lower permanent rate is later established, a subsequent adjustment to the FFR is necessary (except for IHEs subject to 2 CFR 200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revisions result in a balance due NIH of $20,000 or greater, the recipient must submit a revised report whenever the overcharge is discovered, regardless of time since original due date, and post the refund to the PMS document if funds not expired. Refunds under $20,000 on closed PMS documents should be sent directly to PMS with instructions to post to Miscellaneous Receipts. Revised expenditure reports adding previously unreported expenditures should be submitted electronically with an explanation and actions to preclude recurrence: no later than one year from due date for annual FFRs and no later than 60 calendar days from due date for final FFRs (i.e., 180 days from project end date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and use of unobligated balances
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of unobligated balances is determined by award terms; using 'first in-first out,' unobligated funds carried over are expected to be used before newly awarded funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If upon receipt of the annual FFR available funds exceed the NIH share of the approved budget for the current budget period, the GMO may: (a) in response to a written recipient request, revise the current NoA to authorize spending excess funds for additional approved purposes, or (b) offset the current or a subsequent award by an amount representing some or all of the excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient reporting of subrecipient data (FFATA requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most recipients of new Federal funds must report sub-awards/subcontracts/consortiums equal to or greater than $30,000; subaward reports are submitted in SAM.gov and are published on USASpending.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must register with SAM.gov, collect necessary data from subrecipients, and file reports by the end of the month following the month in which the pass-through entity awards any subaward > $30,000. To promote consistency, agency data sources may pre-populate reports; recipients must confirm pre-populated data and provide additional required information. Reports may need to include names and total compensation of the five most highly compensated officers if statutory thresholds are met. Recipients may be required to verify Organization UEI, Name and Address, Parent UEI, Assistance listing number, FAIN, and Federal Awarding Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention reporting under Bayh-Dole and iEdison use
rubrics_metrics.description: Bayh-Dole Act reporting requirements are at 37 CFR 401.14 and recipients must indicate in each competing application and non-competing continuation progress report whether any subject inventions were made and whether they were reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must submit annual invention utilization reports for subject inventions to which title has been elected and for inventions licensed but not patented (research tools). Failure to comply may result in loss of patent rights, withholding of funds, or other enforcement actions. Bayh-Dole permits electronic reporting (37 CFR 401.16); NIH requires electronic reporting through iEdison (Interagency Edison).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Conflict of Interest (FCOI) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Information related to FCOI reporting requirements is contained in Public Policy Requirements -- Financial Conflict of Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must follow the FCOI policy and reporting procedures referenced in NIH public policy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research security requirements (CHIPS/NSPM-33 alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: In alignment with the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 and NSPM-33, NIH has established requirements to strengthen research security across NIH-funded projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH has implemented a series of requirements; recipients should review relevant NIH research security policy sections for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH disclosure requirements for senior/key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: All individuals designated as senior/key personnel in an application must certify and submit information to assist reviewers and NIH staff in making recommendations and funding decisions; details are in the NIH Disclosure Table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply with disclosure terms may cause NIH to disallow costs, withhold further awards, suspend grants, or take other corrective actions; potentially criminal violations will be referred for investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program (MFTRP) eligibility restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals who are a current party to a Malign Foreign Talent Recruitment Program are not eligible to serve as a senior/key person on an NIH grant or cooperative agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must ensure senior/key personnel are not participants in MFTRP per CHIPS and Science Act requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Security Training (RST) certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each senior/key personnel listed on an NIH application must certify they have completed Research Security Training within 12 months of the date of application submission; individual certification is required at time of application via the Biographical Sketch in SciENcv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant institutions must certify that covered individuals employed by the institution and listed on the application have completed RST. The AOR certifies institutional compliance by signing the face page of the application. Completion and certifications required for applications with due dates on or after May 25, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period and access rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients generally must retain financial and programmatic records and other grant-related records for 3 years from the date the annual FFR is submitted; for SNAP awards the three-year period is calculated from the date the FFR for the entire competitive segment is submitted. Federal institutions must retain records for 3 years from the date of submission of the annual FFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR Part 200.334 for exceptions (e.g., litigation, claims, audits requiring longer retention). Retention applies to paper and electronic records; electronic systems must assure stability, reliability, integrity, and accurate representation of originals. NIH, pass-through entities, Inspectors General, Comptroller General, and authorized representatives have rights of access to records for audits, site visits, interviews, etc. NIH's right of access lasts as long as records are retained; pass-through entities must not impose additional access requirements on subrecipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of audits
rubrics_metrics.description: An audit is a systematic review to determine whether internal accounting and other control systems provide reasonable assurance that: financial operations are properly conducted; financial reports are timely, fair, and accurate; the entity has complied with applicable laws/regulations/grant terms; resources are managed economically and efficiently; desired results/objectives are being achieved effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH recipients (other than Federal institutions) are subject to audit requirements in 2 CFR Part 200 Subpart F and NIHGPS provisions when 2 CFR does not directly apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit coverage threshold and submission locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered organizations expending $1,000,000 or more per year under Federal awards are required to have an annual audit per 2 CFR Part 200.501. The Exhibit maps recipient types to source of audit requirement and where to submit audit reports (State & Local Governments, IHEs, Non-Profits, Hospitals -> Federal Audit Clearinghouse; For-Profits/Foreign -> Audit Resolution Division).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If awards are under one program, recipients may elect a single organization-wide audit or a program-specific audit (subject to 2 CFR Part 200.507 and prior written NIH IC approval for program-specific audits). For foreign and for-profit recipients see specific NIHGPS chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the audit reporting package
rubrics_metrics.description: The reporting package must contain: financial statements and schedule of expenditures of Federal awards; independent auditor’s report including opinion on financial statements and the schedule of expenditures of Federal awards and a report on compliance and internal control; a schedule of findings and questioned costs; and, if applicable, a summary of prior audit findings and a corrective action plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data collection form (SF-SAC) and a copy of the Single Audit reporting package must be submitted electronically to the Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC). A senior-level representative must sign a statement included with the data collection verifying compliance and accuracy. Indian tribes may opt out of FAC publication (with responsibility to submit reporting package directly to pass-through entities). If findings relate to HHS/NIH awards, FAC will provide copies to NEARC, OIG, HHS. Thresholds for questioned costs are in 2 CFR Part 200.516.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit resolution and recipient response timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must follow a systematic method to ensure timely and appropriate resolution of audit findings and recommendations; recipients usually are allowed 30 days from the date of request to respond to the responsible audit resolution official concerning audit findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit timely responses may result in cost disallowance or other NIH/HHS actions. At completion of audit resolution the recipient will be notified of the Action Official’s final decision which may be appealed under NIH/HHS grant appeals procedures when applicable. Refunds owed due to audit disallowances must be made according to instructions from the Action Official or OFM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement and contracting for audit services
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient procures audit services, procurement must comply with procurement standards of 2 CFR Part 200, including obtaining competition and making efforts to use small/minority/women/veteran-owned firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations should include all audit requirements and selection criteria. Written agreements with auditors must specify rights and responsibilities of each party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for delinquent or noncompliant audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must submit required audits within time limits specified in 2 CFR Part 200, Subpart F. If recipients are delinquent, NIH may take actions that result in the loss of Federal funds. No audit costs will be allowed as indirect or direct costs to Federal awards if required audits have not been completed or not conducted in accordance with Subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies may request additional audits necessary to carry out responsibilities under law/regulation which will build upon the independent auditor's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific award conditions and remedies for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with award terms and conditions (including confirmed research misconduct) may cause NIH to take actions depending on severity/duration of non-compliance. NIH generally will afford an opportunity to correct deficiencies unless public health/welfare concerns require immediate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may place specific conditions on awards, preclude future awards for a period, impose closer monitoring, withhold funds, suspend or terminate awards, or take other enforcement actions consistent with statutes, regulations, and policies.
